newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Gutnick rules out acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Gutnick rules out acquisitions.

text.p: Australian gold magnate Joseph Gutnick on Thursday ruled out acquisitions by his stable of mining and exploration companies for at least five years.

Gutnick, chairman or chief executive of nine public companies led by gold miners Great Central Mines Ltd (GCM) and Centaur Mining and Exploration Ltd, said they did not need a purchase to ensure growth.

He told a business luncheon in Melbourne the average cost of gold discovery by GCM and Centaur, which now boasted a combined resource base of 10.2 million ounces, was around half the industry average of A$30 per resource ounce.
Gutnick, who came close to financial ruin after the October 1987 stock market crash, also vowed on Thursday to keep a decade-old promise to stay away from share trading.
"Maybe I will increase some of my stakes in some of the companies as time goes along, however no company funds have gone to any purchase of shares and will not," he said.
"You have to stick to where you are successful and we know where we haven't been successful."
"We are not share traders, we're gold explorers and gold miners...," he added.
"I have learnt my lesson from '87 and I don't want to be tempted, even think of entertaining that idea again."
Gutnick has forecast GCM and Centaur to reach combined annual production of one million ounces within 18 months, from over 700,000 ounces in the current year ending June 30 1997.
About three million ounces of the two companies' combined resource base have so far been converted into reserves.
Gutnick said he expected the bulk of the resources to become reserves.

Over two million ounces of reserves are hedged at around A$600 an ounce, protecting future profitability in an uncertain gold market he said, adding GCM and Centaur had also secured an agreement whereby they were not required to make margin calls.
